calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: On the power play, Detroit is one of the league’s best, but Chicago is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Blackhawks take could cost them.

calls.head: Crash the net vs. Bombs away
calls.body: On shots from in close, Detroit is near the top of the league, but Chicago is one of the worst. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Red Wings to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Detroit found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Detroit usually gets worse looks than most teams. Not tonight: a 10.1% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.0% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 175 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Arvidsson lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Connor Bedard opened the scoring for the Blackhawks early in the first, and that was all they would get. Viktor Arvidsson made it 1-1 for Detroit early in the second. John Gibson stopped Frank Nazar on a penalty shot midway through the period. Lucas Raymond gave the Red Wings the lead on the power play early in the third, and Arvidsson struck again with four and a half minutes left to make it 3-1. Arvidsson completed his hat trick into the empty net with a little over three minutes left.

No fluke here. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Red Wings win about four in five. Spencer Knight kept the Blackhawks in it, stopping 27 of 30. The Wings moved to 6-4-3, still last in the Atlantic, while the Blackhawks fell to 4-9-0, still last in the Central.
